routes.description: Establish that theism offers a better overall explanation by supplying a non-causal ground for contingent reality, a principled ultimate explanatory terminus, and an epistemically coherent account of religious experience and diversity.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the theistic resources jointly provide material explanatory advantages over naturalistic alternatives while meeting challenges concerning brute necessity, experiential unreliability, divine communication, and religious disagreement.

motionBridge.description: Show that theism's combined treatment of contingent reality and religious experience makes it the better overall explanation relative to naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Require a non-causal and non-necessitating explanation of the contingent total causal history and identify divine free grounding as the relevant resource.
Provide a principled ultimate terminus whose essence entails existence and explain why a theistic candidate has comparative explanatory relevance.
Justify giving context-sensitive evidential weight to religious experience, testimony, and cultivated religious practices.
Account for ambiguity and religious diversity without requiring that divine communication chiefly produce uniform and detailed theology.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify grounding as the relation by which divine creative activity could unify and explain created causal reality.
Distinguish degrees of experiential and testimonial reliability while preserving qualified trust amid disagreement.

routes.description: Establish that naturalism can match or exceed theism's explanatory coverage without adding God by offering naturalistic foundations for contingent history and explaining religious phenomena through calibrated cognition, social processes, and nonintentional causes.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic accounts cover the principal explanatory domains without a uniquely theistic resource and if the proposed theistic stopping points and experiential expectations do not establish an overall comparative advantage.

motionBridge.description: Show that adding God does not improve the overall explanation once naturalistic alternatives and the comparative costs of theistic explanations are included.

centralBridges.description: Supply a naturalistic structure in which necessary initial reality and indeterministic evolution explain the occurrence of a contingent history.
Require equal scrutiny of naturalistic and theistic ultimate necessities and deny an asymmetry based only on naming a developed divine essence.
Explain why religious experience must be calibrated for ordinary unreliability, cognitive mechanisms, and the relevant comparison class.
Relate ambiguity, unsuccessful visionaries, and enduring religious diversity to the expectations of intentional divine communication and naturalistic causation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Compare explanatory coverage and simplicity across complete worldviews without double-counting a disputed explanatory deficiency.
Preserve live naturalistic ultimate candidates where present knowledge of cosmic origins does not determine their essential structure.

sections.title: Standards for Comparing Complete Worldviews
sections.rationale: This issue fixes how explanatory coverage, simplicity, uncertainty, and reasonable disagreement bear on the motion, and therefore governs how the more specific causal and experiential disputes contribute to an overall comparison.

sections.title: Grounding and the Explanation of Contingent Causal History
sections.rationale: The debate's principal metaphysical clash concerns whether contingent causal history requires a non-causal, non-necessitating ground or can be explained through necessary natural conditions with indeterministic evolution.

sections.title: Necessary Existence and Explanatory Termination
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether theism supplies a principled ultimate explanatory terminus unavailable to naturalism, or whether divine and natural foundations face symmetrical demands concerning necessity, essence, and bruteness.

sections.title: Epistemic Weight and Naturalistic Calibration of Religious Experience
sections.rationale: Religious experience is a distinct proposed source of comparative support whose force depends on default trust, testimonial and first-person justification, learned practices, cognitive mechanisms, and calibrated unreliability.

sections.title: Divine Communication, Visionaries, and Religious Diversity
sections.rationale: The distribution, ambiguity, and durability of divergent traditions test whether religious phenomena fit intentional divine relationship or nonintentional natural and sociological processes within the competing worldviews.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: Arguments can identify genuine considerations favoring theism or naturalism even when there is no agreed algorithm for uniquely balancing all worldview virtues.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: The contingent total causal history requires a non-causal and non-necessitating explanation, for which divine free grounding supplies a resource not identified within science-oriented naturalism.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: Creation is appropriately understood as grounding: God's creative activity is a more fundamental reality that unifies and explains the created causal world.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-10.proposition: Explanatory inquiry can legitimately terminate in autonomous facts that do not need explanation, with real and nominal definitions providing plausible examples.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: A maximally satisfying ultimate explanation would involve an entity whose real definition or essence entails actual existence, and God is a developed candidate for that role.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Default trust in human cognitive faculties and testimony extends presumptively to the widespread practice of interpreting experiences as encounters with God or supernatural reality.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Religious experience should be construed broadly and weighted by quality, while its first-person character can justify an experiencer's non-neutral stance despite disagreement.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Religious experience need not primarily aim at uniform detailed theology and should instead be assessed through whole traditions, lived effects, testimony, and long-term communal functioning.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: A long-isolated religious tradition may reflect genuine experiences of God interpreted through its inherited framework rather than faculties wholly disconnected from reality.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-01.proposition: Naturalists can construct a comparably explanatory worldview without adding God, regardless of the broad shape of causal reality.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: Comparing explanatory coverage and theoretical simplicity requires judgment and can permit reasonable disagreement rather than yielding an algorithmically decisive result.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-07.proposition: A necessary initial state together with necessary but indeterministic evolution can explain the occurrence of a contingent natural history without an additional non-natural ground.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-09.proposition: Postulating a necessary God does not remove explanatory bruteness unless divine necessity can be explained using resources unavailable to the naturalist.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: A naturalist can nominate the universe's initial state as an entity whose essence includes existence, so that explanatory structure does not uniquely favor theism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: A broad category of religious experience is readily explained naturalistically, while a narrower evidentially stronger category raises doubts about how frequently such experiences occur.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: Human faculties are not trusted without qualification; experience teaches the circumstances in which each faculty is unreliable.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: The disorder and ambiguity of religious experience fit nonintentional causes better than communication from an agent intending relationship with human beings.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: The enduring diversity of radically different religious traditions resists a plausible single-religion account and is easier for naturalism to explain.
